A $\mathrm{B}^+$ tree with $\mathrm{L}$ leaf nodes has $\mathrm{L}-1$ keys in internal nodes.

questions.html:
In a $\text{B-tree},$ we store both keys and record pointers in the internal and leaf nodes, but in a $\mathrm{B}^+$ tree, we store the record pointers in the leaf nodes only.

The main advantage of $\mathrm{B}^+$ trees over $\mathrm{B}$ trees is that $\mathrm{B}^+$ trees allow us to pack in more tree pointers to the internal nodes by removing pointers to data, thus increasing the fanout and potentially decreasing the depth of the tree.

Leaf node of $\mathrm{B}^+$ tree has one block pointer which points to the sibling to the right of the tree.

Given that the block size is $1 \mathrm{~K} \;\text{bytes},$ data record pointer is $\text{7 bytes}$ long, the value field is $\text{9 bytes}$ long and a block pointer is $\text{6 bytes}$ long.

If we use $\text{B tree}$ index, then the maximum number of record pointers that can be stored in the index of height $1$ is $\mathrm{X}$, whereas If we use $\mathrm{B}^+$ tree index, then the maximum number of record pointers that can be stored in the index of height $1$ (i.e. two levels) is $\mathrm{Y}$, then $\mathrm{Y}-\mathrm{X}$ is _______

$\text{P}(6) + (\text{P}-1)(9+7) \leq 1024$
So, $\text{P} = 47$
Now :
We want MAXIMUM number of KEYS in a $\text{B-Tree}$ of order $m$ of height $h :$
In such a tree, each non-leaf node would have the maximal number of children $(m),$ and thus the maximal number of keys $(m-1).$
Thus, we would have: (In the below formula, $h$ is number of levels. )

$\text{For B}^+ \;\text{Tree :}$

Let $\text{P}$ be the maximum number of tree/block pointers per internal node. So, we have :
$\text{P}(6) + (\text{P}-1)(9) <= 1024$
So, $\text{P} = 68$

Let’s find the maximum number of keys per leaf node :
Let $\text{K}$ be the maximum number of record pointers/keys per leaf node. So, we have $:6 + (\text{K})(16) \leq 1024$

To get maximum number of keys, we have root node full, so we have $68$ nodes on second level which all are leaf nodes, each having maximum $63$ keys, so $63  \ast 68 = 4284.$
Hence, answer is $4284 - 2208 = 2076.$

questions.html:
Consider a Ordered file with number of records $r=300000$.

Let ordering key field is $\text{9 bytes},$ block pointer is $\text{6 bytes;}$

  • Disk block size $=\mathrm{B}=4096$ bytes.
  • File records are fixed size and unspanned.
  • Record length $=\text{R}=100 \;\text{bytes}$

The I/O cost, in terms of maximum number of blocks needed to fetch into main memory in worst case, when there is NO index over the file is $\mathrm{X}$ and the $\mathrm{I} / \mathrm{O}$ cost when there is single level primary index built for the file is $\mathrm{Y}$. Then $\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{Y}$ is _______
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 42)

  • Ordered file with records $r=300000$
  • Disk block size $=\mathrm{B}=4096$ bytes
  • File records are fixed size and unspanned
  • Record length $=\text{R}=100$ bytes
  • Blocking factor $\text{bfr}=[\text{B / R}]$ (lower ceiling) $=4096 / 100=40$ records per block

The number of blocks needed for the file $=[\mathrm{r} / \mathrm{bfr}]$ (upper ceiling) $=300000 / 40=7500$ blocks
A binary search on the data file $=\log_2(7500)($ upper ceiling) $=13$
Let ordering key field is $\text{9 bytes},$ block pointer is $\text{6 bytes};$ total $\text{15 bytes}$ in each entry of index file bfr for index file is $4095 / 15$ (lower ceiling) $=273$

Total number of index entries $=$ total no of blocks

  • The number of index blocks $=[7500 / 273]$ ( upper ceiling) $=28$
  • To perform binary search on index file: $\log_2(28)$ (upper ceiling) $=5$

To search for a record, we need one additional access to read the data block, thus we need $5+1=6$ block accesses using a binary search Whereas, we need $13$ block accesses without an index file.

questions.html:
Consider an empty $\text{B}^+\;\text{Tree}$ with order $5$ for every node, i.e. there are at most $5$ pointers per node (i.e. at most $4$ keys per node). The records with key values as even numbers from $100$ to $202\; (\text{i.e.} \;100,102,104, \ldots, 202)$ are inserted into the $\text{B}^+\;\text{tree}$ in some order such that each leaf is full.

The maximum and minimum number of nodes that are possible in such $\mathrm{B}^+\;\text{tree}$ are $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ respectively. Then $\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{Y}$ is _______
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 49)

In the leaf level, there will be $\lceil 52/4 \rceil =13$ nodes.
So, we need $13$ pointers at the second last level.
So, for maximum number of nodes, we will put minimum pointers per node and for minimum number of nodes, we will put maximum pointers per node.

  • For maximum number of nodes : on second last level, we have $13 / 3=4$ nodes(With pointers occupancy 3,3,3,4). And one node at root level(With pointers occupancy 4).
  • For minimum number of nodes : on second last level, we have $13 / 5=3$ nodes(With pointers occupancy 5,5,3). And one node at root level(With pointers occupancy 3).

So, $\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{Y}=1$

The height $=2.$

NOTE:

For Maximum Nodes calculation, If you got $5$ nodes in the second last level, then it is Wrong.

For Maximum Nodes calculation, If you are having 5 Nodes in the second last Level, How will you put 13 pointers in these 5 Nodes?? 

Pointers occupancy 3,3,3,3,1  ??? 

But NOTE that Every B+ tree node (except root) must ALWAYS have at least 50% pointers occupancy.. So every node (except root) must always have at least 3 pointers. 

Source solution 2 (score: 13)

Order p: $5$  

Max pointers/children: $5$  

Min pointers/children (non-root): $\lceil 5/2 \rceil = 3$  

Total Keys: Even numbers from $100$ to $202$ is $52$ keys.  

Leaf Node Configuration: Every leaf is full. A full leaf has the maximum number of keys, which is $p-1 = 4$.  

Number of Leaf Nodes: $52/4 = 13$ leaf nodes.  

The number of leaf nodes is fixed at $13$ for both cases, the difference between $X$ and $Y$ comes from the number of internal nodes (including the root).  

Minimum Number of Nodes $Y$:  
We have $13$ leaf nodes. Max children per internal node = $5$.  
Minimum parent nodes = $\lceil 13/5 \rceil = \lceil 2.6 \rceil = 3$.  
The distribution: $(5,5,3)$ which is valid since all $\ge 3$.  
These $3$ internal nodes need $1$ root.  

$Y = 13 + 3 + 1 = 17$.  

Maximum Number of Nodes $X$:  
We have $13$ leaf nodes. Min children per internal node = $3$.  
Maximum parents = $\lfloor 13/3 \rfloor = 4$.  
Distribution: $(3,3,3,4)$. Valid since all $\ge 3$.  
These $4$ internal nodes need $1$ root.  

$X = 13 + 4 + 1 = 18$.  

Thus we obtain: $X - Y = 18 - 17 = 1$
